title: Sensitivity of Nucleation Thermodynamics and Kinetics to the Treatment of Long-Range Interactions
authors: Fernanda Sulantay Vargas, Kimia Sinaeian, Amir Haji-Akbari
abstract: Nucleation rates are exponentially sensitive to the thermodynamic driving force and can therefore depend strongly on the treatment of long-range intermolecular interactions. Here, using the Lennard--Jones (LJ) system as a benchmark, we combine molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, jumpy forward-flux sampling (jFFS), and free-energy calculations to quantify the effect of potential truncation on melting thermodynamics, homogeneous crystal nucleation kinetics, and computational cost. Within the cutoff-radius range $2.5σ\le r_c\le 6σ$, the melting temperature at zero pressure varies by approximately 11%, while the nucleation rate changes by approximately ten orders of magnitude. By invoking classical nucleation theory (CNT), we show that this pronounced kinetic sensitivity originates primarily from cutoff-induced changes in the chemical potential difference between the liquid and crystalline phases. Building on this observation, we develop a CNT-based framework for extrapolating finite-cutoff rates to the full-potential limit and for estimating the expected rate deviations at other cutoff radii and temperatures. These findings also provide a systematic basis for cutoff selection: the optimal cutoff should minimize computational cost while keeping the deviation from the full-potential rate within acceptable bounds. At $kT/ε=0.5$, $r_c=4σ$ provides a reasonable compromise according to these criteria. We further demonstrate that conventional homogeneous tail corrections do not offer a reliable alternative, as they cannot consistently account for the liquid, crystalline, and interfacial environments present during nucleation. Our findings highlight the need to specify and validate the truncation scheme as an integral component of force-field development in simulations of nucleation and other interfacial phase transitions within inhomogeneous environments.
summary: This work rigorously investigates the artificial sensitivity of nucleation rates to the cutoff radius used for long-range intermolecular interactions in the Lennard-Jones model. The study finds that the kinetic rate changes drastically with $r_c$, necessitating a systematic, theory-guided framework to extrapolate results to the full-potential limit. It emphasizes that the choice of truncation scheme must be treated as a fundamental convergence parameter in simulations of phase transitions.
main_problem: The paper quantifies how the calculated nucleation rates and melting thermodynamics are artificially sensitive to the method used to truncate long-range intermolecular interactions.
main_result: The nucleation rate exhibits extreme sensitivity, changing by about ten orders of magnitude when varying the cutoff radius, suggesting that the choice of cutoff is a critical, non-trivial parameter in simulations.
method: The study combines Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations, jumpy forward-flux sampling (jFFS), and free-energy calculations, utilizing Classical Nucleation Theory (CNT) to analyze the cutoff dependence.
model_or_system: The benchmark system is the Lennard-Jones (LJ) fluid undergoing homogeneous crystal nucleation into an Fcc structure. The potential is truncated at a cutoff radius $r_c$, leading to the need for careful long-range corrections.
key_observables: Melting temperature ($T_m$), homogeneous crystal nucleation rate ($R_{hom}$), and the chemical potential difference between liquid and crystalline phases.
important_parameters: The cutoff radius ($r_c$) is the primary variable, tested in the range $2.5\sigma \le r_c \le 6\sigma$. The simulation is run at $kT/\epsilon = 0.5$.
main_assumptions: The authors assume that the kinetic sensitivity stems primarily from cutoff-induced changes in the chemical potential difference ($\Delta\mu$) between the liquid and crystal phases, and they develop a framework to extrapolate finite-cutoff rates.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate reversible paths in the p-T plane for thermodynamic integration, and show the cutoff dependence of the melting temperature and nucleation rate.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of long-range interaction truncation, applies MD/jFFS to the LJ system to calculate thermodynamics and kinetics across various $r_c$, derives the kinetic sensitivity from $\Delta\mu$, and proposes a CNT-based framework for extrapolation and optimal cutoff selection.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluid dynamics, the rigorous treatment of convergence parameters ($r_c$) and the development of extrapolation frameworks are highly relevant to any simulation involving long-range forces, including those encountered in quantum many-body systems or complex quantum field theories.
